subject: research/swe-cachecost
professional: a senior ML-systems researcher who works on LLM serving and agent cost (prompt/KV caching economics, provider cache-write and cache-read multipliers and TTLs, cost-per-task analysis of agentic coding traces such as SWE-bench runs); first checks: is every rate in the price card the provider's published rate for the model actually used, do the component shares and slopes recompute from the raw token counts, is the analysis frozen to a reproducible snapshot, does the fitted context model actually account for the observed super-linear slope, does it look at the TTL choice (1-hour vs 5-minute writes) that drives the write share, and is prior work on agent cost and prompt caching cited

evidence.correctness: The code computes what it says, but the headline split rests on a wrong price. (a) Reproduction: `python3 experiments/run.py` on today's tree gives 4,248 records through 2026-11-19 (no date cutoff), so I fetched the merge commit of PR #8821 (`git fetch --depth=1 origin 704e2970...`, `git archive ... prompts/runs prompts/pricing.json research/swe-cachecost`) and reran run.py on that snapshot: 895 vs 893 records; shares, section D medians, section E and every slope point estimate identical to results.txt (cost vs requests 1.159, reads 1.364, C0 59,873 vs 59,888, g 1,868 vs 1,867). (b) My own script (scratchpad swe-cachecost/indep.py, does not import swe_cachecost) on the same snapshot reproduces cost slope 1.159, read slope 1.364, tool-call slope 0.943, 1.111 calls/request, cost/request $0.034/$0.036/$0.059, start share 76.2%, and cost_usd equals tokens x pricing.json (median ratio 1.0000, 99.8% within 1%). (c) Rate card vs Anthropic's published pricing page (platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing.md, fetched 2026-11-19, line 31) and the Claude API skill models table: every row used matches except claude-sonnet-5-5 cache reads, $0.20 in prompts/pricing.json:14 vs published $0.10 (0.05x input); 853 of 895 runs are Sonnet 5.5. Re-priced at the published rate the median shares are cache reads 29.5% (README 45%), 1-hour writes 52.2% (README 41%), output 16.5% (README 13%): the order of the two largest components inverts. Reads+writes stay 83.5% and the cost slope moves only to 1.175, and all token-only results (95.8% hit share, context model, token slopes) are unaffected. A pricing check against the provider document fails on the lead finding, so 2.
evidence.completeness: Everything listed exists and runs: cc.py helpers, run.py sections A-F printing results.txt (21 s), figure.py writing context_per_request.svg, 5 tests as stated, live page https://marisstella.app/research/swe-cachecost/ returns 200. Reproduces at its merge commit (within the 2 records added by the PR's own run record). Not reproducible from the current tree because run.py reads the growing prompts/runs log with no date cutoff (today: n 4,248, output share 20.5%, g 1,225), which the Limitations section half-acknowledges ('reads the checkout of 2026-10-20'). Next steps (split the starting context, subagent accounting) are listed as future work, not claimed.
evidence.verification: `python3 -m unittest discover tests -v`: 5 tests OK in 0.000 s. Seeded 5 mutants with quality_mutate.py: price column swap in cost_shares caught; bootstrap upper index 0.975 -> 0.5 SURVIVED; quantile() always returning the median SURVIVED (it produces every 10th-90th band in section A); R2 replaced by r SURVIVED; dropping the requests>0 guard in totals() SURVIVED. run.py, which holds the context model (section F), the bootstrap for g and the binning, has no test at all, and no test pins any results.txt number. 4 of 5 mutants survive.
evidence.craft: Read src/swe_cachecost/cc.py (78 lines), experiments/run.py (81), experiments/figure.py (35), tests/test_cc.py (42). Small and readable. Defects: run.py:10-15 globs the live log with no date or commit cutoff, so results.txt cannot be regenerated; run.py:67-80 re-implements the bootstrap inline instead of reusing slope_ci and indexes bs[25]/bs[974] as if exactly 1,000 resamples survived; figure.py duplicates run.py's loading/filtering; cc.py:72 percentile index int(0.975n)-1 is asymmetric with the lower one; tokens_total is dead code outside the tests; README:7 says costs are 'recomputed here from prompts/pricing.json' but sections B-D use the stored cost_usd (run.py:36,49,57); they agree to 1e-4, so no number changes.
evidence.claims: Checked 9 claims. Backed by results.txt and reproduced: 893 records, 95.8% hit share, slopes 1.36/0.63/1.16, 1.11 calls per request, context C0 about 60,000 and g about 1,900 (1,500-2,200), 76% at the median run, cost per request bins, limitations (API-equivalent, R2 0.31, one repo). Not backed: (1) README:9 and the live page, research/README.md:660 and docs/posts/2026-10-30-start-here-how-the-agent-fleet-is-measured.md:27 say cache reads are 45% and the largest component; at the published Sonnet 5.5 rate they are 29.5% and 1-hour writes are the largest (52%); the same wrong price was found in the free-modelcost audit on 2026-11-12 and is still in prompts/pricing.json:14. (2) README:13 'Output grows fastest (slope 1.36 against requests)': cache reads are 1.364 vs output 1.359 against requests, a tie. (3) README:10-11 'a starting context re-read every request explains the shape': the fitted model (C0 59,873, g 1,868) implies a local log-log slope of total reads of (C0+g n)/(C0+g n/2) = 1.24 at the median n=20, vs the observed 1.36, and R2 is 0.31; it explains part of the slope, not the shape. (4) Headline '86%' is the sum of two medians; median of the per-run sum is 87.3% (83.5% at published prices), harmless.
evidence.fitness: A researcher gets a short descriptive decomposition of one harness's own run logs (five days, one repository, 95% one model) with run-level totals only, so cache misses cannot be separated from genuinely new context and nothing about TTL or compaction can be tested. Nearest prior work, none cited: Anthropic's prompt-caching documentation and pricing page (the 1.25x/2x write and 0.05x-0.1x read multipliers the study depends on); Gim et al., 'Prompt Cache: Modular Attention Reuse for Low-Latency Inference' (MLSys 2024) and Zheng et al., SGLang/RadixAttention (2024) on prefix reuse; Kapoor et al., 'AI Agents That Matter' (2024) on reporting agent cost; SWE-bench cost-per-resolved-task reporting. The finding that agentic coding cost is dominated by cached-prefix tokens is the expected consequence of those pricing schemes rather than a new result. One session deep, not part of a programme in research/PROGRAMMES.md, well below the research/CLAUDE.md PhD+ bar; useful as an internal note for this repository's own budget.
evidence.domain: The token accounting (reads/1h writes/5m writes/output) and log-log slopes with bootstrap intervals are standard and done correctly. An ML-systems reviewer would stop at the rate card first (Sonnet 5.5 reads at 2x the published price), then note that with correct prices the largest lever is the 1-hour write premium (2x input vs 1.25x for 5-minute writes, or a keep-alive on the 5-minute TTL, which Anthropic's own caching guidance discusses), which the study never examines even though it observes 5-minute writes are zero; would ask for per-request traces rather than run totals before fitting a context-growth model; would reject reading the OLS intercept on per-request averages as 'the starting context' without checking it against an actual first-request cache write; and would ask for the prior art above.

verdict: A small, readable decomposition of this repository's own agent-run costs that reproduces exactly from its merge commit (895 vs 893 records, every point estimate equal) and whose token-level results (95.8% cache-hit share, the 60,000-token starting context, slopes 1.36 for reads and 1.16 for cost) recompute independently. But its lead finding uses a wrong rate: prompts/pricing.json prices Sonnet 5.5 cache reads at $0.20, and Anthropic's published price is $0.10. Re-priced, cache reads are 29.5% of the median run's cost, not 45%, and 1-hour cache writes (52%) are the largest component. That changes the study's own question of where a cheaper run must save, and the wrong figure is repeated on the live page, the research index and a blog post. Four of five seeded bugs survive the tests, run.py has no date cutoff, the context model accounts for a read slope of 1.24 against 1.36 observed, and no prior work is cited. Correctness, claims and verification are below 3, so it does not meet the bar. It is finished as a one-session note, far below the PhD+ research bar.
